name: 1623 Farnam
notes: Omaha's carrier hotel: a nine-story, ~75,000 sq ft facility with around 8 MW of capacity at 1623 Farnam Street downtown, home to the OmahaIX internet exchange and some 60 carriers. News Press & Gazette Co. subsidiary Berks Group acquired Nebraska Data Centers and the 1623 Farnam carrier hotel in 2018 and established 1623 Farnam LLC — so 'Nebraska Data Centers' as an operator name is HISTORICAL, not current. Build-out history: a $10 million expansion in 2019 built out the fifth floor, floors six through nine were added in 2021, and the final two data halls completed in June 2025 added 1.5 MW of IT capacity and space for 280 racks. CEO Bill Severn cites 'significant demand from AI workloads, edge deployments, content platforms, and broadband networks'. The company is separately planning an OMA2 campus expansion explicitly aimed at AI and edge infrastructure growth, with no site, size or date disclosed on its own page — a LEAD to re-check, not yet a proposable facility. DCD also reports the facility serves Trump Media & Technology Group; that is a tenant claim DCD attributes to other reporting and is deliberately NOT recorded as a structured field. capacityMw is the ~8 MW total, not the 1.5 MW increment; investmentUsd records ONLY the sourced $10M 2019 fifth-floor expansion, since no total site capex is published. Coordinates are a street-address approximation.

notes: 5C Group (formed May 2025 when Hypertec Cloud acquired 5C Data Centers) owns/builds the campus in the Prime Ohio corporate park; Vultr (legal entity The Constant Company, LLC) is the AI/cloud tenant. Corrects a discovery-pipeline conflation of this project with a separate, independently tax-credited Crusoe Energy Systems project elsewhere in Springfield -- not the same facility. Multi-building campus — renderings show up to four buildings; second, third, and fourth buildings referenced at groundbreaking. Capacity MW not publicly disclosed. Investment described as 'multi-billion dollar' — no firm figure confirmed; field omitted per policy. Construction jobs described as 'thousands'; permanent roles as 'hundreds of high-quality long-term positions' — projections only, numeric fields omitted. Aligned is exploring on-site nuclear power (SMRs) for this campus and nearby Zanesville/Cambridge sites; no agreement confirmed. Coordinates approximate (village-level). Site infrastructure funding note: the Coshocton Port Authority received a $58.7M grant (Ohio Dept of Development All Ohio Future Fund, announced July 21, 2025) for utility upgrades, water/wastewater extensions, and roadway improvements across the broader industrial park — this benefits Aligned indirectly but is not a direct subsidy to Aligned and is therefore not listed under subsidies.

Construction targeted to begin by end of the decade (~2029-2030); operations/first power targeted 2030s (one Energy Northwest source cites mid-2030s). generation_notes: Amazon announced funding (2024-10-16) for the feasibility/environmental/safety/permitting/licensing phase of four Xe-100 reactors with Energy Northwest and X-energy, amid AI-driven power demand. Energy Northwest owns, builds, and operates the facility; X-energy is the reactor-technology licensor. Amazon holds a contractual right to purchase power from the first 320 MW phase; public power utilities may purchase up to 50% of the full 960 MW build-out per Energy Northwest's own project page, so Amazon's offtake share of the full build-out is not necessarily 100%. Design-builder Cascade Nuclear Partners (Kiewit Nuclear Solutions / Black & Veatch / Aecon) selected 2025. Amazon separately anchored a ~$500M Series C-1 investment in X-energy (announced 2024-10-16, alongside Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Citadel's Ken Griffin, Ares Management affiliates, NGP, and the University of Michigan) supporting X-energy's reactor design/licensing and Phase 1 of its TRISO-X fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, TN -- this is company-level X-energy funding, not Cascade project capex. Project-level construction jobs are projected at ~1,000-2,000 and operational jobs at ~100-200 per Energy Northwest's own project page; these are the operator's projections, not delivered/operational counts, and are recorded here as notes rather than in the jobs field.

notes: Distinct from CleanSpark's ten existing Tennessee sites; Mountain City is in Johnson County in the far northeast corner of the state. STATUS IS UNSETTLED AND THE SOURCES CONFLICT: WUOT (2025-08-15) reports city leaders 'beginning to back down' after threats of legal action, while Baxtel's undated summary says the Board of Mayor and Aldermen approved a zoning change and lists the facility as planned for 2027 and still needing further approvals. The utility promised roughly $170,000 in additional annual city tax revenue. Baxtel says CleanSpark plans immersion cooling to mitigate noise; that is a stated intent for an unbuilt site and is deliberately NOT recorded in the mining.coolingType field. energy_notes: The Colorado Sun reports CoreSite will draw from the Xcel grid rather than building its own generation; the fully built three-phase development would draw 65 to 75 MW, with phase one about 18 MW. community_notes: Elyria-Swansea residents have opposed the project over water use, air pollution and noise since construction began, holding a neighborhood press conference in February 2026; the backlash helped prompt Denver's one-year moratorium on new data center approvals, passed by city council in May 2026, which blocks CoreSite's two additional planned buildings but not the one already standing. Generator startup testing in July 2026 drew complaints from neighbors at the adjacent Viña Apartments and from Tepeyac Community Health Center; a local science teacher won a community grant to measure infrasound at the site.

energy_notes: Behind-the-meter, primary-plus-backup on-site generation dedicated to the campus; explicitly not exporting to ERCOT.
generation_notes: TCEQ Standard Permit Technical Review (Registration 177263, approved 2025-01-22) confirms 10 simple-cycle turbines — 5x Solar Titan 350 (~38 MW) + 5x GE LM2500 (~34.1 MW) = 360.5 MW — behind-the-meter for on-site compute, no grid export. A proposed expansion (major TCEQ permit filed Jul 2026, not yet approved) would add 41 turbines (~1.4 GW) plus 18 diesel gensets; the ~1.2 GW figure often cited for the campus describes IT/interconnect capacity, not generation nameplate. Gas-plant buildout cost reported at ~$500M, distinct from the ~$1.1B data-center project figure.
emissions_notes: NO per-pollutant annual tonnage is recorded here, deliberately. This is a TCEQ Electric Generating Unit Standard Permit registration — a rule-based authorisation that does not state per-pollutant tons-per-year ceilings the way a PSD or plan-approval permit does. The only annual tonnages in the file are the applicant's own calculated potential-to-emit (Table 1(a) of the modification application, built from manufacturer rates and AP-42 emission factors), and potential-to-emit is not a permitted ceiling; this project does not publish one as the other. The enforceable limit the standard permit does impose is a RATE: 0.14 lb NOx/MWh for units operating more than 300 hours per year, against which the application estimates a controlled rate of 0.09 lb/MWh. Registration history: originally registered 2024-08-30 for six Titan 350 plus six GE LM2500; the modification approved 2025-01-22 reduced each model from six to five, giving the ten turbines above (Titan 350 site-rated 38 MW each, GE LM2500 34.1 MW each). Registered as Abilene DC 1, LLC dba Crusoe Energy Systems (Regulated Entity RN112029079, Customer CN606295137). A separate major TCEQ permit application filed July 2026 seeking roughly 41 additional turbines is NOT covered by this registration and none of its figures are recorded here.
emissions_unitsCovered: ten (10) natural gas-fired simple cycle combustion turbines: five Solar Titan 350 (TURBINE-1 through TURBINE-5) and five GE LM2500 (TURBINE-6 through TURBINE-10)

Crusoe historically used on-site flared natural gas but divested those operations; Warrenton campus is grid-connected via Ameren Missouri — no on-site gas generation reported here. Distinct from the Google/Crusoe 'Goodnight' campus in Armstrong County TX.

name: CyrusOne Dugway Proving Ground Data Center
notes: Conditionally selected, currently in exclusive negotiations with the US Army (not finalized); expected completion ~2029. Would be CyrusOne's first Utah facility, developed in partnership with Carlyle. Framed as AI-driven Army infrastructure ('AI is a strategic asset... force multiplier' per the Army Secretary) rather than marketed as a standalone AI-brand product. Coordinates are approximate. In exclusive negotiations with the US Army as of the cited source. Subsidies checked at the municipal tier (2026-09-05): no site-level subsidy found. — structural, not merely unresearched: Dugway Proving Ground is U.S. Army-owned federal land in unincorporated Tooele County, which sits outside any county/municipal property-tax roll, so a Title 17C Community Reinvestment Agency increment or abatement is not possible here regardless of county policy. Any public-sector instrument would be a federal Army real-estate arrangement, not a local or state subsidy, and the site remains in exclusive negotiations, not a finalized agreement. Utah's EDTIF programme excludes data centres and the UCA 59-12-104 exemption is self-executing.

name: Digihost / Digi Power X — Fortistar North Tonawanda
notes: 1070 Erie Ave, North Tonawanda, NY. 60 MW operating with potential for another 60 MW unbuilt. Under an unresolved legal/regulatory cloud: a NY Supreme Court ruling (Nov 2024) required the Public Service Commission to complete a CLCPA climate-impact review of the site's power-plant-sale approval; the NY Appellate Division, Third Dept affirmed that ruling on May 28, 2026 — the required CLCPA review remains incomplete as of this writing, and the facility continues operating pending it. The company (now "Digi Power X," ticker DGXX) has filed for Planning Commission approval to convert the site to an 80,000 sq ft AI/HPC data center, but this is blocked by North Tonawanda's data-center moratorium (imposed July 2024, extended again ~June 2026 after resident pushback) — the AI pivot is a real, filed proposal, not vaporware, but has no live AI hosting revenue at this site. A New York statewide bill (Responsible Data Center Development Act, S10642/A11560) passed both legislative chambers June 4, 2026 and remained unsigned/pending before Gov. Hochul as of July 2026; it would impose a one-year moratorium on new permits for large (≥20MW) data centers. This would be a second, largely redundant obstacle behind North Tonawanda's own binding local moratorium, which already blocks the AI/HPC conversion described above.

The operator field records DOE as the landowner and solicitor, NOT as the eventual data-center operator, which is unknown. Oak Ridge is one of four federal sites DOE identified for AI infrastructure. Distinct from the existing Kairos Power Hermes 2 record, which is a separate NRC-licensed reactor project at Oak Ridge.

name: EdgeConneX MCN New Albany (South Campus)
notes: EdgeConneX's ~$1B multi-phase "MCN New Albany" South campus. Per the Ohio Tax Credit Authority scope-of-work filing: Phase I converts a ~525,000 sq ft existing warehouse (9850 Innovation Campus Way) into an 80 MW data center; Phase II proposes two new 72 MW facilities (144 MW) — capacityMw.planned = 224 (80 + 144, IT load). A co-located PowerConneX natural-gas energy center (reported 140–216 MW of generation across sources) is EXCLUDED from capacityMw as on-site generation, not IT load. Footprint spans the South PropCo 2 parcels (~97 ac incl. the built anchor) plus the adjacent North PropCo 1 parcel (3356 Clover Valley Rd NW, 170 ac); ~267 ac combined. "MCN" is EdgeConneX's internal project prefix (not publicly decoded). Distinct from EdgeConneX's separate Piper Farms parcel (~5 mi away) and from edgeconnex-ashville-oh (Pickaway County). Public-reception check (2026-09-10): IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: this is EdgeConneX's New Albany/Licking County campus (Innovation Campus Way; Phase 1 120MW, Phase 2 216MW, Phase 3 430MW). It is a SEPARATE EdgeConneX project from the heavily-opposed EdgeConneX proposal in Ashville, Pickaway County, OH (denied annexation 2026-02-02 after packed council meetings and a Change.org petition) -- do not merge that record's contention into this one. For New Albany/Licking County specifically, a land-purchase article (2025, checked 2026-09-10) mentions only general Central Ohio-wide concern that data centers could raise electricity costs, immediately caveated because this project's power comes from dedicated on-site generation (PowerConneX), not the residential grid. No hearing, resident testimony, or official statement specific to this Licking County site was found.

energy_notes: Initial generation: on-site natural gas. Fermi acquired 600MW+ of gas turbines in two deals (July 2025): 478MW from Firebird LNG/Siemens Energy (six SGT800 turbines + heat recovery steam generators + one SST600 steam turbine) and 135MW from GE 6B Frame units acquired from a New Jersey facility. TCEQ issued preliminary approval for up to 6GW of combined-cycle gas (November 2025); air permit secured February 2026 after ~279 public comments. Long-term plan adds four Westinghouse AP1000 reactors (~4.4GW nuclear baseload; COLA filed June 17 2025, NRC accepted two of three parts for review September 2025, Part 3 deadline December 31 2026, first reactor targeted 2031, all four by 2038) plus solar and battery storage. Fermi is also evaluating SMRs (MOU with Doosan Enerbility). Entire campus is behind-the-meter — private grid, no public utility offtake.
community_notes: TCEQ air permit process (for 93 planned gas turbines) drew 279+ public comments, majority opposed. 63 contested case hearing requests filed before State Office of Administrative Hearings; 21 additional public meeting requests. Primary opposition group: Panhandle Taxpayers for Transparency. Key concerns: air quality (modeled 2,140 tpy CO and 1,591 tpy NOx), water demand, impacts on farmland and nearby cattle operations (Tyson Foods facility adjacent). Fermi bused in college students to a December 2025 public meeting, stoking further controversy.

notes: SEPARATE SITE from IREN Sweetwater (Nolan/Fisher County — do not conflate). Full 750 MW figure is total campus transmission capacity; the AI/Microsoft Horizon 1–4 build-out comprises four 50 MW IT (75 MW gross) liquid-cooled data halls = 200 MW IT total, targeting end-2026 delivery. Horizon 1 (50 MW IT / 75 MW gross) energized Q4 2025 — operational; Horizons 2–4 remain under construction as of mid-2026. Coordinates approximate (county seat area). Site is a 576-acre freehold parcel with on-site 345 kV substations connecting directly to ERCOT. Investment for Horizon 1–4 reported as $300–350M (range; not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd). Microsoft contract ($9.7B total, 5-year through ~2031) covers NVIDIA GB300 Blackwell Ultra GPU cloud services; 20% upfront prepayment funded capex. Dell Technologies hardware supply agreement: $5.8B. IREN also holds a separate NVIDIA cloud services contract at Childress. Rack density 130–200 kW per rack; projected PUE 1.05–1.10. Approximately 25 current full-time local employees, 50+ expected at 750 MW full build-out; over 500 contractors during construction phase (approximate reported figures — omitted from jobs numeric fields). IREN Community Grants Program distributes $250,000 annually to the Childress area.

Coordinates are approximate (geocoded from a listed street address, not parcel-confirmed — the ~800-1,000-acre campus could place any specific building up to ~1-2 miles from this point). Jobs: Meta states 'more than 1,000 construction workers at peak' and 'approximately 100 permanent jobs' — approximations from press release, not firm figures; omitted from numeric fields. Phase 2 expansion (375 additional acres west of original parcel, developer Atmoss LLC) proposed but withdrawn March 2026 before city council vote. Coordinates approximate (near 11th St & Creek Turnpike, East Tulsa).

The campus itself broke ground in 2018 and has been operating since 2021; Meta's current info sheet still describes operational buildings there. Operating campus and paused expansion phase are two different things, and this record tracks the campus. Recommend keeping status operational and recording the 2022 partial-expansion pause as statusHistory context rather than a status change. Alabama's Data Processing Center incentive program has no per-company reporting requirement, and neither the state nor its agencies publish which data center operators receive abatements or in what amount. Meta is named as a beneficiary of the sales-tax exemption but no dollar figure attaches to it. This is a DISCLOSURE GAP, not a GASB 77 audited negative: I did not obtain any municipal ACFR tax-abatement note this run, so it does not establish that a particular city has no agreement with a particular operator. Any future subsidies entry for an Alabama site will most likely have to come from a city or county resolution rather than from a state source.

Houses the NOAA-funded Orion supercomputer — a Dell-EMC system described at its 2019 ribbon-cutting as 28 cabinets, 72,000 processing cores and 350 TB of RAM at 5 petaFLOPS, then the fourth-fastest system in U.S. academia. MSU separately broke ground in May 2023 on a 35,000-square-foot, $45 million High Performance Computing Data Center in the same park, expected to be finished in 2025; no source read this session confirms that building's completion, so it is NOT recorded as a separate facility and no capacity is asserted for it here. Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap building point for the High Performance Computing Collaboratory at 2 Research Boulevard. Distinct site from cspire-starkville-ms, which is a commercial colocation facility elsewhere in the same park.

Recorded under onSiteGenerationMw as dedicated captive generation, but note the S-1 calls the plants "neighbouring": they sit ~5 miles south of Piketon adjacent to the DOE site, are developed by "an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary", and SB Energy "do[es] not expect to own or operate" them. Ohio Power Siting Board case 26-0746-EL-BGN (applicant Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC) covers only a first tranche of "up to 2 gigawatts"; AEP Ohio transmission (new 765 kV Baku-Gavin line and four substations) is a separate docket. AEP grid capex is stated as $4.2B by DOE and ~$5.1B in the S-1, unreconciled. CAUTION: the project site states the gas generation "will be owned by the U.S. Government", but the S-1 says "no binding agreement has been executed between us or any of our affiliates and any governmental entity with respect to the funding, construction, ownership or operation of the generation facilities" - do not assert federal ownership. Only ~0.8 GW of gross load has contracted utility service so far.
community_notes: Documented local support alongside contamination-legacy distrust. Support: State Sen. Shane Wilkin - "It’s just going to be a generational change for this area"; SODI executive director Steve Shepherd called it "a model for the country"; the Scioto Valley-Piketon Area Council of Governments chair framed it as moving contaminated residential land to industrial use. Concern: a neighbouring farmer with contaminated property ("This is the most contaminated place around here"), and Conserve Ohio on water, transmission and the precedent of siting hyperscale projects on legacy DOE land. No litigation, moratorium or public-hearing defeat found as of 2026-09-01; a statewide watchdog notes this project lacks the named opposition groups seen elsewhere in Ohio. Community money (not a public subsidy to the operator): a $40M Community Benefits Agreement from SB Energy plus an incremental $40M from OpenAI.

The permit's project description states the engines 'will power generators providing primary power for the site's two (2) new data center buildings' — this is dedicated on-site generation, not a merchant plant. 72 x 3271.8 kW is about 235.6 MW of gross engine nameplate; Grist reports the plant as 200 MW, which is the figure recorded here. Permitted potential emissions total 997,261 TPY CO2-equivalent, 51.28 TPY NOx, and 202.72 TPY CO. Grist reports Novva turned to self-generation because Rocky Mountain Power could not supply the campus until 2031, and that Novva sought a two-year Clean Air Act exemption in March to run diesel generators while the gas plant is built. name: Project River Data Center
notes: THE DATA-CENTER TENANT IS NOT CONFIRMED. Wright Brothers Construction CEO Mitchell Simpson told Mix 104.1 WCLE on 2026-08-26 that the power plant is certain but its offtaker is not: "We definitely know we're developing a power plant... We don't know what it's going to power yet... It potentially could be a data center, but it very well could be something else," naming advanced manufacturing, robotics and semiconductor manufacturing as alternatives, before adding that with that much power "it's very likely going to be that." The company's own 2026-08-26 release describes the campus as "anchored by an on-site power plant and data center." Recorded at confidence 'reported' for that reason. Roughly 850 acres of privately-owned Wright family land west of I-75 and north of Old Lower River Road NW, along the Hiwassee River in northern Bradley County near I-75 Exit 33, submitted for rezoning and annexation into the City of Cleveland on 2026-08-25. The $11.3bn headline is the whole campus; $7.3bn is the data-center portion as itemised in press coverage. Groundbreaking is not expected until end of 2027 and the build is phased over 60 months. Coordinates are a geocode of Lower River Road NW, not the parcel; no source states lat/lon. No state or local incentive agreement is named in any of the three sources.

CEO Mitchell Simpson told Mix 104.1 WCLE the biomass process yields 200 gallons per minute of usable internal water for cooling loops and that the plant needs no river intake or discharge pipes. Classified closed_loop on the recirculating-circuit rule; the sources do not state the heat-rejection equipment.
energy_notes: Powered behind the meter by the co-located Project River energy campus (500 MW biomass plus 1,000 MW natural gas), with a requested 360 MW TVA interconnection for backup and peaking only. Developers say no diesel generators.

name: Rattlesnake Creek Wind Project
notes: 320 MW / 101-turbine wind farm in Dixon County, northeast Nebraska, between the towns of Allen, Emerson and Wakefield — about 100 miles from the data center it serves. Built by Enel Green Power with $430 million of local investment; generates around 1,300 GWh/year, avoiding a reported 940,000 tons of CO2 annually. Enel's own project page states the plant powers Facebook's (Meta's) Sarpy data center — the named generation behind the '100% renewable' claim on meta-sarpy-springfield-ne, whose notes reference 'a wind farm in Dixon County' without naming it. Meta's own Sarpy info sheet independently states 'A Meta-supported project is adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy in Nebraska', matching this project's nameplate exactly. Facebook's initial contracted share was 200 MW of the 320 MW, with the remaining 120 MW to other buyers and Adobe holding a 10 MW slice; Facebook was reported to take the full output over time. Originally conceived by Kansas-based Tradewind Energy in 2013. This is a contracted PPA resource on the grid, NOT behind-the-meter generation. Coordinates are an approximate centroid of the Allen/Emerson/Wakefield project area, NOT a turbine-array geocode. CAVEAT on 'primary is not current': the operator field records Enel Green Power as stated on the project's own live page fetched this session; Enel's US renewables portfolio has been subject to divestment activity industry-wide, so present ownership should be re-verified before publishing.

name: Riot Platforms Corsicana Facility
notes: Phase I (400 MW) operational for Bitcoin mining with immersion cooling. AMD contracted 50 MW for HPC workloads. Riot developing 112 MW Core and Shell infrastructure at Corsicana for future hyperscale AI tenants. Campus acquired in phases to 858 total acres. ERCOT-approved for 1 GW total. Navarro County's October 2024 abatement records cite a considered $640M investment and 140 new jobs; the signed agreement sets a $380M minimum taxable value and 140 FTE by January 1, 2026 (a Riot spokesperson separately cited 180 jobs). Re-tagged from data_center to crypto_mining (2026-07-10): the operational 400 MW is Bitcoin mining (current majority use); the 600 MW AI/HPC evaluation remains at proposal stage, not built. Riot does not disclose hash rate per-site (only company-wide EH/s spanning Corsicana + Rockdale + Kentucky), so hashRateThPerS is left unknown here rather than misattributing a company total. Miners are MicroBT ASICs designed for immersion cooling. ERCOT demand-response/curtailment participation (Four Coincident Peaks program) is a structural, revenue-generating part of Riot's operating model company-wide (~$21M in Q1 2026 curtailment credits), so power arrangement is tagged "mixed" rather than plain grid.

name: Sovereign Gazelle Bitcoin Mining Data Center
notes: Texas-based Sovereign Global Solutions Inc. (CEO Kevin Mohan, also affiliated with Big Star Blockchain, a bitcoin-data-center services firm) bought 15 acres at 369 Union Road for $300,000 in August 2025; incorporated the project entity 'Sovereign Gazelle' in April 2026. Plan: a 50MW bitcoin mining data center occupying 10 of the 15 acres. Build depends on easements from four neighboring landowners for 75-ft utility poles carrying the 50MW line — all four have refused as of June 2026. Morgan County Commission passed a 12-month moratorium on bitcoin-mining data centers on 2026-06-23 after resident petitions (450+ signatures) citing noise/air-quality/property-value concerns. VoltCore is the EPC/engineering contractor for the power buildout, not the site owner/operator — do not attribute operatorship to VoltCore. County officials describe the project as 'still pursuing' but stalled pending right-of-way. STATUS RE-CHECK, NO CHANGE - proposed remains correct. Morgan County adopted a unanimous 12-month data-center moratorium in June 2026, but the area is unzoned and the county has since said it cannot stop this site; the project's only forward movement found is negotiating utility easements. No building permit, construction start or cancellation was found, so the record should not move in either direction. The moratorium and the county's stated inability to enforce it against this parcel are recorded here as context.

(c) capital cost has moved from "$6.3 billion a year ago" to "$11 billion" to "$19 billion"; the GCEDC-published $19.46B is used. Hochul was considering a moratorium measure that could block it entirely. Flag for hand review: record explicitly as 'requested', not granted. SUBSIDY NOT RECORDED AS A FIELD (maintainer adjudication 2026-09-10): reporting describes a REQUESTED package worth about $1.46bn from the Genesee County IDA for the STAMP site, not an awarded one — at the time of the 2026-07 reporting the Governor was weighing a moratorium measure that could block it entirely. The `subsidies` schema has no granted-versus-requested distinction, so publishing the figure there would present unawarded money as awarded. name: Switch Pyramid Campus
notes: Steelcase Pyramid campus, Gaines Township, Kent County MI (south of Grand Rapids; NOT the city of Wyoming, which is a separate municipality ~5 km north). Total campus target: 1.8M sq ft, 320 MW, ~$5B investment across all phases. Phase 1 (225,000 sq ft white space) and Phase 2 (312,000 sq ft) operational; Phase 3 in planning/early construction as of 2025. Michigan's largest data center by capacity. Coordinates are approximate Pyramid campus location on East Paris Ave, Gaines Township. Status re-check, NO change proposed - but flagging a possible mislabel for a maintainer. This record has the oldest basis in the state (lastUpdated 2025-01) and sits at 'under_construction' while the campus itself has been open and serving customers since 2017, with buildings added incrementally. I did NOT propose 'operational' because the only opening evidence I could fetch predates the record's own 2025-01 basis, so the maintainer may have chosen 'under_construction' deliberately to track the ongoing second/third-building expansion. Deciding this needs a maintainer's intent, not more sources. No cooling or water source was fetchable; switch.com/pyramid renders its specs via JavaScript and returned only a headline.

name: Endicott Bitcoin Mining Pilot
notes: Texas-based TA Infrastructure filed a permit application to place Bitcoin-mining computers, collectively drawing 1.4 MW, inside a shipping container on a gravel pad at oil producer Hilcorp's Endicott field on Alaska's North Slope, powered by natural gas from Hilcorp's existing generators. energy_notes: Existing 2,514 MW two-unit (BWR) plant, operating since the 1980s. Up to 1,920 MW earmarked for AWS via a front-of-meter retail power supply PPA through 2042 (announced 2025-06-11), ramping from 840-1,200 MW by 2029 to 1,680-1,920 MW by 2032. This front-of-meter structure replaced the original co-located behind-the-meter arrangement after FERC rejected that interconnection service agreement 2-1 on 2024-11-01; transition expected after transmission reconfiguration, targeted spring 2026.
community_notes: American Electric Power (AEP) and Exelon formally intervened at FERC against the co-located behind-the-meter ISA amendment, arguing it could shift up to $140 million/year in transmission costs onto PJM ratepayers as a 'free rider' benefit -- a factor in the ISA's rejection. This is a regulatory/ratepayer-cost dispute among utilities, not local community opposition; the front-of-meter restructuring addresses the underlying jurisdictional issue.
generation_notes: AWS bought Talen's co-located 'Cumulus' data center campus (land, power infrastructure, powered shell) for $650 million, announced/closed around March 2024. Talen and AWS have also stated intent to explore new small modular reactors (SMRs) in Talen's PA footprint and plant uprates to add net-new PJM capacity -- exploratory, not a committed project. Talen projects roughly $18 billion in total contract revenue over the life of the expanded 1,920 MW/through-2042 supply agreement (contract value, not capex).

notes: Built on the site of the former coal-fired Somerset Generating Station (shut 2019/2020). Address 7725 Lake Rd, Barker, NY — coordinates are a town-level geocode, not a confirmed parcel pin (approximate). TeraWulf holds exclusive access to up to 750 MW of site infrastructure capacity. The AI/HPC pivot here is a SIGNED, revenue-generating deal, not speculative: two 10-year HPC colocation agreements with Fluidstack (buildings CB-3 42MW + CB-4 162MW, later expanded with CB-5 +160MW) worth $3.7B in contracted revenue, backed by a $1.8B Google backstop and Google equity stake (~14% pro forma). Tagged mixed_use since Bitcoin mining (145MW) remains the larger operational segment versus HPC (60MW energized as of Mar 2026), but the AI/HPC business is real and growing, not aspirational. A New York statewide bill (Responsible Data Center Development Act, S10642/A11560) passed both legislative chambers June 4, 2026, imposing a one-year moratorium on new permits for large (≥20MW) data centers; it remained unsigned/pending before Gov. Hochul as of July 2026. Facilities with construction already underway are exempt, so TeraWulf's current build here is likely grandfathered, but any future unbuilt expansion phase requiring new permits could be affected if the bill is signed before construction starts. CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no fields. Lake Mariner has NOT applied to the Niagara County IDA for assistance, so there is no PILOT or IDA agreement to find for this site — the county manager says so on the record. This closes off the IDA lane for this facility specifically. Also worth recording for context: Fluidstack is named as a tenant using the site alongside TeraWulf.

name: Buckeye Tech Corridor
notes: Master-planned data center park on a ~2,069-acre former residential (Cipriani) parcel Tract acquired for ~$136M, south of I-10 in Buckeye; planned for up to ~20M sq ft across as many as 40 data centers at full build-out over ~15 years (~$20B). Coordinates are an approximate town-level geocode (Buckeye, south of I-10), not a parcel-confirmed point. The City of Buckeye executed a development agreement with AZLCO Buckeye, LLC (Ordinance No. 08-24, adopted unanimously 2024-08-06). It reimburses the developer for six enumerated regional infrastructure components it builds and dedicates to the city — two public-safety sites, temporary and permanent public-safety facilities, $15M toward the Johnson Road interchange, and oversized regional water infrastructure — funded by 20% of the tax revenue the project itself generates, beginning only after the city has received $60M cumulatively and terminating 20 years from the effective date. It is capped at "the lesser of" the developer's verified costs or $50,000,000, so it cannot exceed what the developer actually spent; it is cost recovery for public infrastructure rather than an incentive, abatement or credit, and is therefore not recorded as a subsidy. Nothing has been paid to date. Buckeye's economic-development director has projected "more than 360 jobs at full build out" — an end-state across as many as 40 separate future data centers, none yet leased, permitted or built, and so not recorded as a permanent-jobs figure for this site. A search of 226 Buckeye Council and P&Z agendas (Feb 2024 – Aug 2026) found no GPLET and no Foreign Trade Zone instrument.

generation_notes: Ward 250 is a 100-kWt TRISO-fueled, helium-cooled high-temperature gas reactor (HTGR) test unit at the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab. It achieved full-power fueled criticality on 2026-06-18 — the first DOE-authorized advanced reactor built and operated independently outside the national-laboratory system — and was used to power an NVIDIA DGX Spark AI chip in a public demonstration. The design is intended to scale to a 5 MW unit. NVIDIA has announced plans for a future AI factory in Emery County tied to this site; no timeline given.

name: La Osa Data Center Park
notes: Vermaland LLC is a Phoenix-area land developer and land-banking company (CEO Kuldip 'Ken' Verma, founded 2006, controls ~25,000 acres of metro Phoenix land). DCD explicitly noted 'it is unclear whether Vermaland would operate its own data center facilities' — Vermaland plans to sell or rent parcels/buildings to tenants. No end tenants or hyperscaler operators have been named as of July 2026. Original plan: 59 data centers, up to 3 GW capacity ceiling, up to $33B investment ceiling, 3,300-acre site south of Eloy along the Greene Canal. A separate adjacent 1,700-acre parcel already holds Industrial-2 zoning for data centers, gas plants, battery storage, and solar. After strong public opposition (all ~60 public comments opposed), operator announced May 2026 scale-back to 11 data centers and 1 GW ceiling. Board of Supervisors hearing scheduled August 26, 2026; no permits issued as of record date. notes: 500MW on-site gas-fired data center campus (~200-600 acre portion of a larger ~600-acre Tooele Valley Public Infrastructure District development that also includes a truck stop, hotel, and warehouses near I-80); backed by Utah Inland Port Authority financing. Developer plans a reverse-osmosis plant discharging ~250,000 gallons/day of brine into Great Salt Lake wetlands, drawing significant local opposition. Subsidies checked (2026-09-08): no site-level subsidy confirmed for this parcel. A $4.875M Utah Inland Port Authority Infrastructure Bank loan was reported in April 2024 to Zenith Bolinder, LLC — the Delaware LLC that petitioned UIPA in March 2024 to create the Tooele Valley Public Infrastructure District, representing 100% of surface property owners within it, and which KSL describes as "a partnership with longtime Utah developer Zenith Development"; Charles Akerlow appears both as the petition's contact sponsor and as Zenith Development's managing director. The two are affiliated but are not the same legal entity, the loan terms were not confirmed against a primary document, and the district's boundary exhibit is a scanned image that could not be read — so whether that loan reaches this data-centre parcel is unresolved. UIPA's executive director stated in July 2026 that the authority's involvement covers transportation within a 600-acre portion and does not extend to the southern section planned for the data centre.
